title: Glucose teaching note
snippet: Glucose is the main blood sugar the body uses for energy. A common fasting teaching interval for adults is 70 to 99 mg/dL. A result above that band is high in this note, and a result below it is low. One value does not diagnose diabetes or low blood sugar.

title: HbA1c teaching note
snippet: HbA1c reflects the share of hemoglobin with sugar attached over the prior few months. A common teaching interval is 4.0 to 5.6 percent. This note uses that band only to describe the supplied numbers. It does not diagnose diabetes.

title: Creatinine teaching note
snippet: Creatinine is a waste product filtered by the kidneys and measured in blood. A broad adult teaching interval is 0.6 to 1.3 mg/dL. Muscle mass and the lab method change what a single result means. This note does not diagnose kidney disease.

title: eGFR teaching note
snippet: eGFR is an estimate of how much blood the kidneys filter each minute. This teaching set marks a band of 60 to 120 in the standard filtration unit. A clinician reads the estimate with age, creatinine, and the equation that was used. This note does not diagnose kidney disease.

title: LDL cholesterol teaching note
snippet: LDL cholesterol is a blood fat often tracked on a lipid panel. This teaching set uses a band of 0 to 100 mg/dL. Diet, medicines, and other fats change how a clinician reads the number. This note does not set a treatment goal.

title: HDL cholesterol teaching note
snippet: HDL cholesterol is another blood fat reported beside LDL. This teaching set uses a band of 40 to 60 mg/dL only to mark the supplied interval. A clinician decides what a higher or lower result means for a person. This note does not call a result healthy or unhealthy on its own.

title: Triglycerides teaching note
snippet: Triglycerides are fats in the blood that rise and fall with meals and metabolism. This teaching set uses a band of 0 to 150 mg/dL. A recent meal can change the result. This note does not diagnose a lipid disorder.

title: TSH teaching note
snippet: TSH is a pituitary signal that tells the thyroid how much hormone to make. A common teaching interval is 0.4 to 4.0 uIU/mL, and mIU/L uses the same numbers. Pregnancy, medicines, and illness can shift the result. This note does not diagnose a thyroid disorder.

title: Hemoglobin teaching note
snippet: Hemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. A broad adult teaching interval is 12.0 to 17.5 g/dL. Altitude, pregnancy, and the lab method change the band a clinician uses. This note does not diagnose anemia.

title: WBC teaching note
snippet: WBC counts the white cells in a volume of blood. A common teaching interval is 4.5 to 11.0 thousand per microliter. Infection, stress, and medicines can move the count for a short time. This note does not diagnose an infection.

title: ALT teaching note
snippet: ALT is an enzyme found mostly in the liver and reported as an activity level. A common teaching interval is 7 to 56 U/L. Exercise and medicines can raise it for a short time. This note does not diagnose liver disease.

title: AST teaching note
snippet: AST is an enzyme found in the liver, heart, and muscle. A common teaching interval is 10 to 40 U/L. The same person can have a different ALT result on the same day. This note does not diagnose liver or muscle disease.
